output.summary: The project team discusses the redesign of a remote control to reduce production costs from 25 Euros to 12.50 Euros. They decide to use normal batteries instead of kinetic energy or a hand dynamo. The Industrial Designer changes the remote's shape from a double curve to a single curve to reduce costs. The team removes the number buttons one through nine to save 4.50 Euros and drops the speech recognition feature to save 4 Euros, despite the popularity of speech recognition among users. They retain the LCD screen. The team replaces all separate buttons with a single integrated scroll-wheel push-button. The remote is made of hard plastic with a special color applied to the casing. They eliminate the sponge-like material from the design. The final design includes a single-curved plastic case with one integrated scroll-wheel button and an LCD screen. The team evaluates the remote's match to young user behavior as a 3 out of 7, visibility of relevant functions as a 5 out of 7, technological innovation as a 2 out of 7, and ease of use as a 6 out of 7, resulting in a final evaluation score of approximately 3.11. They name the product 'The Real Remote' and add a speckled pattern to represent the special color. The team agrees that their interaction and collaboration improved significantly after the first meeting and felt there was room for creativity despite strict financial limitations. Marketing considers the digital pen more effective for their work than the Smartboard screen.
